title: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX
description: A UNIQUE INDEX both speeds up lookups AND enforces that no two rows can share the same value - it's actually what a UNIQUE constraint uses behind the scenes. Create a unique index named `idx_products_name_unique` on `products.name`.
hints: 💡 SQL concept to consider: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX

Same shape as a normal CREATE INDEX, with UNIQUE inserted right before INDEX - Postgres then rejects any INSERT or UPDATE that would create a duplicate value in that column, exactly like a UNIQUE constraint would.
Name the index idx_products_name_unique, make it UNIQUE, on the products table, over the name column.
expected_behavior: Creates a unique index on products.name - fast lookups by name, and duplicates are now rejected.
solution: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_products_name_unique ON products (name);
explanation: A UNIQUE constraint (like the one added with ADD CONSTRAINT ... UNIQUE earlier) and a UNIQUE INDEX end up doing the same enforcement - in fact, adding a UNIQUE constraint automatically creates a unique index for it under the hood.
